A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UnSeenTimeQA with the same title, authors, and underlying benchmark. All 28 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original context-alteration experiments, human web-retrieval results, nine-model benchmark evaluations, and depth/duration analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, context-alteration and knowledge-cutoff comparisons, and a quantified analysis of GPT-4o reasoning errors.

M1.justification: The logistics-plan generation, random event durations, template rendering, event tracking, answer conventions, and zero-shot chain-of-thought approach remain. v2's interlinked-dictionary description and explicit propagation of delays clarify existing hypothetical-event reasoning rather than establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations on RealTimeQA, FreshQA, and TAQA, covering current and post-cutoff factual questions, plus TempReason's Time-Time task. The original three benchmarks and UnSeenTimeQA's logistics domain, question types, and serial/parallel scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 replace Gemma-2B/7B and Llama-3-8B/70B with Gemma-2-9B/27B and Llama-3.1-8B/70B. GPT-4o remains, while Mistral-7B, Phi3-7B, Gemini-1.0-Pro, and GPT-4 leave this comparison. v2 additionally compares two GPT-4 versions in the new knowledge-cutoff experiment.

E3.justification: v1 randomly samples 250 questions per question type and difficulty; v2 samples 20 at each depth from 6–20, producing 300-question splits. Total reported samples change from 12,000 to 10,800. The new cutoff comparison uses 150 questions per benchmark anchored in 2023 without context. The reported web-search annotator count changes from two to three.

E4.justification: v2 adds a four-category error analysis of 60 GPT-4o failures each from hard serial and parallel tasks, with examples and first-error classification in Section 7/Figure 5. It revises the depth analysis and removes v1's duration-sensitivity analysis and Figure 4; that analysis is not relocated to an appendix.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 change aggregation from four random-sampling repetitions in v1 to three sampled splits in v2. Mean accuracy and standard deviation remain the reporting practice. Neither version supplies seed values, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces TempReason's gold-context accuracies: Event-Time changes from 27% to 66% and Event-Event from 26% to 69%, without explaining the revisions. Tables 2–3 are substantially replaced under changed sampling and model settings; GPT-4o's hard-parallel static accuracy is 58.9% versus 47.33%, not a controlled performance comparison. v2 adds Time-Time's 97%, cutoff-comparison results, and error-category frequencies, while removing per-dataset web-retrieval percentages and duration results.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theorems, proofs, or substantive formal derivations. v2's more explicit positional-depth description restates the existing event-separation measure rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a synthetic TSQA benchmark intended to avoid factual memorization. v2 adds explicit claims of independence from periodic manual updates and knowledge-base updates, sharpens the novelty claim around complex parallel events, and identifies long-range and interlinked-event failures in the abstract.

C2.justification: v1 explains generally better parallel-task performance through reduced arithmetic demands. v2 replaces this with a mixed-performance interpretation emphasizing interlinked dependencies and questioning positional depth as a parallel-task complexity measure. It adds extraction-versus-reasoning explanations, mechanisms associated with the new error categories, and an English-only applicability limitation.

D1.justification: New appendices document event-generation templates and benchmark sources/time ranges. Revised examples provide scenario-specific object inventories instead of v1's repeatedly inconsistent inventories and explicitly state delay propagation. Model endpoints and GPU allocations are updated. Conversely, v2 removes v1's public benchmark repository link and quality-check description; this establishes a disclosure loss, not that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the benchmark against continually updated TSQA resources, discussing RealTimeQA, FreshQA, TAQA, and PAT-Questions. It adds TimeBench's temporal-reasoning taxonomy and co-temporal reasoning work to distinguish its parallel scenarios. v1's positioning through synthetic logical and mathematical reasoning benchmarks is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and results discussion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized around traditional versus post-cutoff benchmarks, data statistics move into Section 4, and the experimental subsections are consolidated. The limitations become connected prose, and the appendices are reorganized while retaining corresponding example and prompt sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is expanded with contexts and parallel-event comparisons. v1's Figure 2 becomes a simplified single-column schematic in v2 Figure 3, losing the six illustrative images. Depth plots are redrawn and stacked; new cutoff, error-analysis, and alteration-example figures appear. Table 1 loses its web column, an appendix dataset table is added, and model-endpoint tables are merged.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies the concrete reasoning-error analysis promised but absent in v1, broadens evidence about existing benchmarks, and improves generation documentation and example consistency. These support a net gain in explanatory value and inspectability. The gain is moderated by narrower model-family coverage, removal of the benchmark access link, and unexplained TempReason score revisions. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement rather than a substantial resolution of the paper's empirical and reproducibility weaknesses.
